reasons: Verified product facts support this first-email scope: Introduce Transistor as a podcast host where a single account can carry more than one show at no extra per-podcast charge, publishing each feed to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and other apps, with per-episode download analytics in the dashboard; the single next step is starting the 14-day free trial and creating a show.
recommendation.eligible_subsegment: Introduce Transistor as a podcast host where a single account can carry more than one show at no extra per-podcast charge, publishing each feed to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and other apps, with per-episode download analytics in the dashboard; the single next step is starting the 14-day free trial and creating a show.
allowed_claims: The Transistor API uses API keys to authenticate all requests, sent via an HTTP header named x-api-key
The Transistor API is built around the JSON:API specification
The API supports sparse fieldsets, letting a request specify only particular fields to return, e.g. fields[episode][]=title&fields[episode][]=media_url
The API supports including a resource's related resources in one request, e.g. include[]=show, and this can be combined with sparse fieldsets
The Get show analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/:id) retrieves downloads-per-day for an entire podcast and defaults to the last 14 days if no date range is given
The Get all episode analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/:id/episodes) retrieves downloads-per-day for all episodes of a podcast and defaults to the last 7 days
The Get single episode analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/episodes/:id) retrieves downloads-per-day for a single episode and defaults to the last 14 days
The Get episodes endpoint (GET /v1/episodes) retrieves a paginated list of episodes ordered by published date, filterable by show_id, query, and status (draft, scheduled, or published)
Episodes can be filtered by status: one of draft, scheduled, or published
Episode list results default to descending order (newest first) and default to 10 resources per page starting at page 0
The episodes list endpoint paginates with a default page number of 0 and a default of 10 resources per page
Starter plan is $19/month, includes unlimited podcasts, 20,000 monthly audio downloads, and 50 private podcast subscribers
Starter plan includes 20,000 monthly audio downloads
Professional plan is $49/month, includes video podcast publishing, 100,000 monthly audio downloads, 500 GB file storage, 500 private podcast subscribers, and dynamic ads
Professional plan includes 100,000 monthly audio downloads
Professional plan includes 500 GB of file storage
Business plan is $99/month, includes 250,000 monthly audio downloads, 1 TB file storage, 3,000 private podcast subscribers, and removes Transistor branding
Transistor offers a 14-day free trial
Transistor does not charge extra for creating additional podcasts on one account
Transistor generates a website automatically for a podcast after choosing a design
Transistor's analytics show average downloads per episode, popular podcast apps, number of subscribers, and trends
Transistor supports private, members-only podcasts for a company or online community
Transistor distributes podcasts to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and many more
Transistor won the Quill Award for Best Podcast Hosting
Stephen Robles says Transistor is his favorite podcasting platform and that HLS video lets him distribute shows in all formats his audience wants from one place

findings.explanation: The campaign directions require this multi-show promise to state the decision-changing Starter conditions: $19 per month billed monthly in USD and 20,000 monthly audio downloads shared across the account. Both are omitted.
The requested action is to start the trial and create the next show; the CTA asks only for trial signup.

findings.text:
For an agency or network, this gives client and internal shows a straightforward home: one account, separate podcasts, and no additional per-podcast charge. Transistor offers a 14-day free trial.

Start your 14-day free trial →
findings.explanation: This sequencing implies access to the advertised multi-podcast operation through the trial route, but no literal source establishes that entitlement during the trial.

decision.summary: The core one-account, separate-podcast and no-additional-per-podcast-charge claims are supported, as is the 14-day trial CTA. Revision is required because trial access to the multi-podcast operation is not established and the draft omits explicitly required Starter pricing, pooled download capacity and the create-your-next-show action.

benefit_retention.explanation: The prior passage's concrete benefit—creating a separate podcast without an additional per-podcast charge—appears directly in the revised email with the same operation and consequence.
benefit_retention.original_passage: Create separate podcasts without an additional per-podcast charge.
benefit_retention.revised_passage: Creating an additional podcast does not add a per-podcast charge.

notes: Email 1 failed automatic checks after repair: "A 14-day free trial lets you create your next show as a separate podcast and see how additional shows sit inside the same account.": E23 establishes a 14-day free trial and E24 establishes additional-podcast creation generally, but no literal source establishes that this capability is available during the trial. The promised trial entitlement and inspection experience therefore remain unresolved.; "If you continue with Starter, $19 per month, billed monthly in USD, includes unlimited podcasts.": The literal sources support unlimited podcasts regardless of subscription plan, but none of the supplied literal quotes states Starter's $19 price, monthly billing basis, or USD currency. brief.interpretation: I interpret “introduce our product to a new buyer” as one acquisition email for a solution-aware agency or network choosing a host for a new show. The email introduces Transistor through a supported product-led proposition: one account can hold multiple distinct podcasts without an additional per-podcast charge. The single next step is to start the 14-day free trial and create the next show.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Network or agency running multiple shows.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (grounded; check applicability): Agencies offering podcast production as a client service, hosting and managing multiple client (or internal) podcasts from one place rather than running each show as a one-off project.
brief.reader_segment: Network or agency running multiple shows
brief.promise: An agency can run more than one podcast in a Transistor account without an additional per-podcast charge.
brief.orientation: Transistor is a podcast hosting platform that publishes audio and video shows to the major listening apps and, on one paid account, lets an agency run more than one podcast without a per-podcast charge.
brief.arc: Show a solution-aware buyer how Transistor structures multi-show hosting, qualify the entry plan’s pooled capacity, then invite them to create one show during the 14-day trial.
brief.sequence_rationale: This is a product-led introduction, so it does not invent a buyer problem or a failing incumbent workflow. It leads with the documented multi-show account structure because that is directly useful to the selected audience, then uses the Starter terms to qualify the commercial promise and the free trial to support the requested action. No unsupported objection or recipient history is required. The single thing that would most change this campaign is a readable copy of the unavailable source page or verification of its missing details.

emails.selection_reason: For an agency or network that may host multiple distinct shows, the ability to add podcasts without an additional per-podcast charge is a concrete reason to consider Transistor. The Starter terms make the account-level price and pooled download condition visible, while the 14-day trial provides a supported first step.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the agency wants to host multiple shows itself, it can keep them as distinct podcasts in one Transistor account without paying an additional per-podcast charge.
value_case.mechanism: Start a 14-day trial and create the next show as its own podcast. Transistor does not charge extra for creating additional podcasts. If the agency continues on Starter, the plan is $19 per month when billed monthly and includes unlimited podcasts with 20,000 monthly audio downloads shared across the account.
decision_conditions: The multi-show proposition applies when the agency wants the podcasts held in one account.
Starter is $19 per month when billed monthly in USD.
Starter’s 20,000 monthly audio downloads are an account-level allowance shared across its podcasts.

claim_conditions: Frame the use case conditionally because the recipient’s current account structure and number of shows are unknown.
Keep the multi-show benefit attached to one account.
State the Starter price only as $19 per month, billed monthly in USD.
Keep the 20,000 monthly audio download allowance at account level; it does not increase with each added podcast.
Start the 14-day free trial to create the account
Create each show as a separate podcast inside that account at no extra per-podcast charge
Submit each show's feed to the listening apps via Transistor's distribution step
Starter plan ($19/month) includes 20,000 monthly audio downloads shared across the whole account, so download allowance is a pooled account-level resource, not per-show
Do not promise: No claim that client users can be restricted to only their own show's dashboard
Do not promise: No claim of a ready-made client-facing analytics or ROI report
Do not promise: No claim about migrating existing shows off an incumbent host without disruption
Do not promise: No claim of headcount or time savings, growth outcomes, or cost comparison against any competitor
Do not promise: No claim that video publishing, dynamic ads or branding removal are available on the trial or on the entry plan
Do not promise: No claim that video publishing, dynamic ads, or branding removal are available on the trial or on the entry (Starter) plan
Do not promise: No claim that the pooled download allowance scales per added show without upgrading plans
This is a documented-use draft, not proof of the broader audience hypothesis or recipient fit.
emails.target_audience: Network or agency running multiple shows
emails.job: Get a new buyer choosing a host for an upcoming show to start a 14-day Transistor trial and create that show.
emails.single_idea: Transistor lets an agency create multiple distinct podcasts in one account without an additional per-podcast charge; Starter includes unlimited podcasts, with its download allowance shared across the account.
emails.mechanism: The reader can start a 14-day trial and create the next show as a separate podcast. Additional podcasts do not carry an extra per-podcast charge. On the $19-per-month Starter plan, unlimited podcasts share the account’s 20,000 monthly audio downloads.
emails.belief_shift: Before: adding another client or internal show may require evaluating another hosting purchase. After: Transistor offers a documented one-account model with no additional per-podcast charge, subject to the plan’s shared account capacity.
must_not_say: Do not claim that client users can be restricted to only their own show’s dashboard.
Do not claim that Transistor provides a ready-made client-facing analytics or ROI report.
Do not claim that existing shows can be migrated from another host without disruption.
Do not claim headcount savings, time savings, audience growth, revenue gains or cost superiority over a competitor.
Do not claim that video publishing, dynamic ads or branding removal are included in the trial or Starter plan.
Do not claim that the download allowance increases for every additional show; plan capacity is shared across the account.
Do not imply that the 14-day trial proves long-term plan capacity or fit.
Do not claim that every agency should own its clients’ hosting accounts.
Do not turn distribution, analytics, API functionality, private podcasts, storage or higher-tier plan features into secondary pitches.
Do not make an exclusivity or superiority claim against Buzzsprout or any other host.
Do not imply automatic placement in every podcast directory.
Do not present this documented use as proof that Transistor fits every agency or network.
emails.objection: Does adding another show mean paying another per-podcast charge, and what capacity does the entry plan provide?
emails.call_to_action: Start your 14-day free trial and create your next show.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Transistor’s one-account structure is a workable way to host the agency’s next show alongside additional podcasts.
emails.next_step_value: The signup starts a 14-day free trial in which the reader can create the next show and inspect the multi-show account structure before choosing a paid plan.
emails.next_step_limit: The trial does not establish client-specific dashboard permissions, migration from another host, or whether the shared download allowance will suit the agency’s long-term combined volume.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the one-account, multiple-podcast model immediately relevant to an agency or network; avoid generic hosting language, unsupported savings claims and claims of competitive uniqueness.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, direct sentences and Transistor’s practical vocabulary: show, podcast, account, publish, distribute and feed. Explain the workflow instead of praising it. Do not add a greeting or sign-off unless the copywriter needs one.

reasons: Verified product facts support this first-email scope: Introduce Transistor as a podcast host where a single account can carry more than one show at no extra per-podcast charge, publishing each feed to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and other apps, with per-episode download analytics in the dashboard; the single next step is starting the 14-day free trial and creating a show.
recommendation.eligible_subsegment: Introduce Transistor as a podcast host where a single account can carry more than one show at no extra per-podcast charge, publishing each feed to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and other apps, with per-episode download analytics in the dashboard; the single next step is starting the 14-day free trial and creating a show.
allowed_claims: The Transistor API uses API keys to authenticate all requests, sent via an HTTP header named x-api-key
The Transistor API is built around the JSON:API specification
The API supports sparse fieldsets, letting a request specify only particular fields to return, e.g. fields[episode][]=title&fields[episode][]=media_url
The API supports including a resource's related resources in one request, e.g. include[]=show, and this can be combined with sparse fieldsets
The Get show analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/:id) retrieves downloads-per-day for an entire podcast and defaults to the last 14 days if no date range is given
The Get all episode analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/:id/episodes) retrieves downloads-per-day for all episodes of a podcast and defaults to the last 7 days
The Get single episode analytics endpoint (GET /v1/analytics/episodes/:id) retrieves downloads-per-day for a single episode and defaults to the last 14 days
The Get episodes endpoint (GET /v1/episodes) retrieves a paginated list of episodes ordered by published date, filterable by show_id, query, and status (draft, scheduled, or published)
Episodes can be filtered by status: one of draft, scheduled, or published
Episode list results default to descending order (newest first) and default to 10 resources per page starting at page 0
The episodes list endpoint paginates with a default page number of 0 and a default of 10 resources per page
Starter plan is $19/month, includes unlimited podcasts, 20,000 monthly audio downloads, and 50 private podcast subscribers
Starter plan includes 20,000 monthly audio downloads
Professional plan is $49/month, includes video podcast publishing, 100,000 monthly audio downloads, 500 GB file storage, 500 private podcast subscribers, and dynamic ads
Professional plan includes 100,000 monthly audio downloads
Professional plan includes 500 GB of file storage
Business plan is $99/month, includes 250,000 monthly audio downloads, 1 TB file storage, 3,000 private podcast subscribers, and removes Transistor branding
Transistor offers a 14-day free trial
Transistor does not charge extra for creating additional podcasts on one account
Transistor generates a website automatically for a podcast after choosing a design
Transistor's analytics show average downloads per episode, popular podcast apps, number of subscribers, and trends
Transistor supports private, members-only podcasts for a company or online community
Transistor distributes podcasts to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and many more
Transistor won the Quill Award for Best Podcast Hosting
Stephen Robles says Transistor is his favorite podcasting platform and that HLS video lets him distribute shows in all formats his audience wants from one place
unresolved_objections: Can I actually stop each client seeing the other clients' shows in that one account?
recommendation.recommended_next_action: Draft this documented use. Treat recipient circumstances as unconfirmed.
recommendation.override_risk: This draft does not establish the broader audience hypothesis or qualify any recipient.
